correctness.rationale: The frozen finding (RESULT.md lines 5–22) takes fixed q>=3, all proportions positive, and independent iid atomless priorities. Uniform priority order can be realized with independent exponential clocks of rate 1/N. At time T an edge whose two endpoints remain unmatched cannot have rung earlier; exponential memorylessness gives exact rate X_iX_j/N for pair i,j, including after conditioning on past occupancy. The scaled coordinate martingale has bracket at most T/N and the bounded-cube drift is Lipschitz, so Doob and Gronwall give convergence uniformly on compact time intervals. To verify the ODE parametrization, write F(g)=prod(1−a_jg) and y_i=a_iF(g)/(1−a_i g). With g'=F(g), differentiation gives y_i'=−y_i sum_{j≠i}y_j, and monotonicity plus F>0 up to its first root forces g to approach 1/a_*. Evaluating the polynomial y_i there gives precisely the unique-largest product and zero in every coordinate for ties. The key horizon comparison is deterministic: every subsequent edge consumes a distinct surviving vertex outside any selected largest part. Thus the change of that part, of the total and of every other part is bounded by twice the minority count at the fixed horizon. Taking N first and then the horizon to infinity proves the classwise terminal LLN even if the finite-N proportions break a limiting tie. Boundedness gives L1 convergence. The 8m,7m,5m example has matching counts 5m,3m,2m and limiting unmatched density 3/160. Direct recursion on labeled feasible edges gave exact finite terminal laws including P(U=2)=1/5 and P(U=0)=4/5 for K_{2,2,2} (python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_math_reproduction.py); neither that calculation nor the supplied verifier's recorded simulation proves terminal asymptotics. The frozen verifier was inspected rather than run.

evidence: The 1986 abstract reports a conservation law for the rate equations and an explicit three-species solution, but does not display its formula.

The inspected greedy matching paper treats regular/high-girth or bounded-degree settings; the dense tripartite catalogue result gives exactly three fixed positive parts, while the dominant-class defects result takes vanishing minority proportions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the cited bounded-degree graph estimates nor either indexed tripartite theorem establishes the fixed arbitrary-q positive-fraction ground regime. Exact overlap of the earlier rate-equation formulas remains possible and is not denied.

evidence: The indexed tripartite law gives the precise product for three parts and uses the same terminal-time comparison in that regime.

With four or more positive parts, grouping parts creates a block with active internal edges and does not give a three-species edge-selection process; nor do rate equations by themselves imply that an infinite-horizon LLN follows from a compact-time fluid limit.
The weighted-tripartite index entry mentions a closed-form law, but its RESULT.md was unavailable in the local mirror; in any case the indexed scope is tripartite.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The q>=4 law, where every class contributes a factor, requires the arbitrary-q solution and a terminal stochastic proof. The exact tripartite match and deterministic antecedents are credited without treating them as a general stochastic theorem.

evidence: Scanning a uniform edge permutation and repeatedly selecting a uniform edge of the unmatched-induced graph give the same accepted-edge law, since each accepted edge leaves a uniform relative order on the surviving edges.
The deterministic limit is an equal-rate multispecies annihilation ODE, but that equation is not by itself a stochastic time-to-absorption statement.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The index's uniform-feasible-edge wording is an exact model equivalence, not a distinct process; continuum rate equations are equivalent only at the fluid level, not as a terminal LLN.

value.rationale: An all-fixed-q terminal formula separates unique-largest and tied-largest regimes and quantifies when irreversible deposition leaves a positive macroscopic vacancy even with a perfect matching available. Its product of all asymmetry factors and terminal-horizon control are useful for comparing heterogeneous complete substrates; the main contribution is the arbitrary-q law, not the already matched tripartite special case or a claim about spatial kinetics or fluctuations.
